query: Among the twenty largest economies (by 2024 dollar GDP), take the one with the lightest public debt burden relative to GDP at the end of 2017. Output prices rose 10.0% and nominal output 13.1% in 2018. Holding the nominal debt stock fixed, by how many points of GDP did the price rise alone lower that burden in 2018?

text.text: Identifies that price rises lower the debt ratio through the nominal-growth term gamma/(1+gamma)=pi/(1+gamma)+g/(1+g), so the inflation part is pi/(1+gamma) times last year's debt ratio.

data.text: Uses WEO nominal GDP and GDP deflator series and general government gross debt (GGXWDG_NGDP, NGDP, NGDP_D).

computation.text: Inflation erosion of debt ratio RUS 2018 = 1.27 pp of GDP

assembled_from: Escolano (2010) A Practical Guide to Public Debt Dynamics (doc 55319ff9-c45c-4e8d-99e4-5562a1158bf2)
provenance.selection: seeded draw over top-20 economies by 2024 USD GDP (frozen), one per country-year

gold_report_note: Published value is WEO series or none; no corpus report states it, nothing to withhold.
distractors: full debt-dynamics decomposition (interest, growth, primary balance)
exchange-rate valuation effect on foreign-currency debt
